extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders who wish to comment on or track an FAA petition for exemption; petitioners and practitioners filing or summarizing FAA exemption petitions
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice summarizing an FAA petition for exemption that describes the relief sought, cites affected regulatory sections, and provides procedural instructions for submitting public comments and accessing the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments identification and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on this petition must identify the petition docket number and must be received on or before January 6, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting a comment, include the docket number (e.g., FAA-2025-2287) on the comment. Ensure timely submission so the comment is received by the stated deadline; late comments may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of comment submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Send comments identified by docket number [FAA-2025-2287] using any of the following methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal (http://www.regulations.gov), Mail to Docket Operations, Hand Delivery or Courier to Docket Operations (Room W12-140) between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday (except Federal holidays), or Fax to (202) 493-2251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions at regulations.gov for electronic filing. For mail or hand-delivery, use the exact address and observe business hours. Fax transmissions should use the provided number. Choose the submission method that ensures receipt by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and public posting of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 5 U.S.C. 553(c), DOT posts these comments, without edit, including any personal information the commenter provides, to http://www.regulations.gov, as described in the system of records notice (DOT/ALL-14 FDMS), which can be reviewed at http://www.dot.gov/privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include personal information you do not wish to be publicly posted. Review the DOT privacy notice and FDMS system of records before submitting. Be aware that comments are posted 'without edit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket access and how to read background documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Background documents or comments received may be read at http://www.regulations.gov at any time. Alternatively, go to the Docket Operations in Room W12-140 of the West Building Ground Floor at 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday (except Federal holidays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for accessing the docket on regulations.gov or visit the physical Docket Operations during business hours to review materials. Use the docket ID to locate relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official PDF and verification against official edition
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format. Only official editions of the Federal Register provide legal notice of publication to the public and judicial notice to the courts under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on the Federal Register for legal research, cite or verify content against the official PDF on govinfo.gov or the official edition. Do not rely solely on the prototype HTML rendition for legal notice or citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements to summarize a petition for exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice identifies: Docket No.; Petitioner; Section(s) of 14 CFR Affected; and a Description of Relief Sought (e.g., what regulatory relief is requested and for what operations). The notice is published pursuant to 14 CFR 11.85.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition summary should include the docket number, petitioner name, specific regulatory sections from which relief is sought, and a clear description of the relief requested (including aircraft/model, types of operations, and purposes). Cite the governing procedural authority (e.g., 14 CFR 11.85).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document headings and metadata to include in Federal Register notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings may contain: the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and each part the document amends or relates to; the agency docket number/agency internal file number; the RIN identifying the regulatory action in the Unified Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Document Drafting Handbook for details on required headings and metadata. Include standard entries like AGENCY, ACTION, SUMMARY, DATES, ADDRESSES, and FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and legal effect statement of the notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this notice is to improve the public's awareness of, and participation in, the FAA's exemption process. Neither publication of this notice nor the inclusion nor omission of information in the summary is intended to affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear statement of purpose and clarify that the summary's publication does not determine the petition's legal status or outcome. This manages expectations of commenters and interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for further inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: For further information contact: Alexander Kem, Office of Rulemaking, Federal Aviation Administration, 800 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20591, at 202-267-9677.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a named contact with office, mailing address, and telephone number so interested parties can obtain additional information about the petition or procedures.
